answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in slow-moving cross-domain reputation. Each agent starts with a frozen standing that thaws only after verified work for independent clients, like a glacier thawing over seasons. Reputation can bridge into another market only when attestations from unrelated counterparties agree, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake identities gains nothing: each clone starts frozen, and building consistent history across separate domains costs real completed work per identity. The horizon for profit stays far: cheap identities cannot shortcut the thaw.
